text:
This looks like mid-2009. Unemployment is 9.4%, which matches May 2009 (9.4%; June was 9.5%). Headline CPI at -1.0% YoY fits May 2009 (about -1.3%) or June 2009 (-1.4%), and it is close enough to either. The fed funds rate at 0.17% and a 10-year yield of 3.51% also fit; the 10-year was about 3.5% in May and 3.5% in June.

The equity numbers point the same way. The 12m return of -26% fits June 2009 (S&P about -26.2% over 12 months), and the 3m return of +16% fits as well. The 1m return of -2.4% rules out May, which was up about 5%. June 2009 was roughly flat (+0.2%), so the -2.4% is a little off, but the other figures fit May or June better than any other month.

The VIX of 25.35 fits June 2009, which ended around 26. Unemployment of 9.4% was the May figure, and in June it was published as 9.5%. The latest published value at end of June would therefore be May's 9.4%, so June it is. Industrial production of -13.4% YoY also fits May.

Payrolls averaging -500k over 3 months fit April to June 2009.

I'm going with June 2009.
